data.name: Elisa: The Innkeeper - Prequel
data.detailed_description:
"If I married all those who said they want me, now I would have so many of those husbands. All men who stay at this inn immediately fall in love with me..." Elisa

Complete Game now Available! Go check it out!

Our visual novel introduces the story of Elisa, a beautiful owner of an inn, struggling with the amorous proposal of honorable Knights, high born Princes and rich Merchants.

It will be the Player to decide Elisa's fate and his/her choices may even influence her destiny for the better or the worse.

The Player is -not- the protagonist of this story, however.

His/Her judgements affect every character and their actions, like a god that watches everything from above. For this reason, every decision is a tough choice to make.

Your choice will change the story forever!

Our Prequel summarizes about 20% of our complete story and features 3 main story branches.

The choices you make take account for the possibility of gaining special items; It's up to you to dicover them and when to use them.

This allows you to influence the outcome of the story in a positive or negative way in specific situations, deciding how the story unfolds.

Of course all of those features will play a much more important role once our story will be available in the future.

The Prequel is just our first step!

Hope you enjoy it!

reviews.review:
Elisa: The Innkeeper: Prequel is a short visual novel that puts me in the role of someone watching over Elisa and deciding how her story develops. Elisa runs an inn where knights, princes and wealthy merchants keep showing up and taking an interest in her. I am not playing as Elisa myself, which is actually a nice change from the usual visual novel setup. Instead, my choices influence the people around her and can push the story in better or worse directions. The whole thing has a simple medieval romance setting, but there is more choice involved than I expected from such a short game.

The choices are easily the best part for me. The prequel has three main story branches and represents roughly 20 percent of the planned full story, so I am not getting a complete adventure here. Even so, the decisions can change what happens and can also lead to special items that I can discover and use at certain points. I like when a visual novel actually gives me reasons to think about my choices instead of making every decision feel like a slightly different piece of dialogue. Here, I at least feel like I am shaping Elisa's future rather than just reading a story from beginning to end.

The presentation is another thing I enjoyed. It has a colourful anime inspired look that fits the light medieval romance setting, and the characters are easy to tell apart. The soundtrack also helps give the scenes a more relaxed feeling. There is some adult content and nudity as well, so this is definitely not something I would describe as a completely innocent romance game. I think the visual style works better when the game is focusing on the characters and their relationships, while some of the more suggestive parts feel like they are there mainly because of the type of visual novel this is.

The biggest problem is the length. This really does feel like a prequel rather than a full game, and I reach the end before I feel like I have seen enough of the characters or the world. The fact that the developers describe it as an introduction to the larger Elisa story makes sense, but it also means I have to accept that a lot of the setup is left hanging. There are eleven achievements and several branches to go back through, but replaying the same early sections only goes so far when the overall story is this small.

I also think the writing could have been stronger in places. The basic idea of watching Elisa's life and influencing her decisions is interesting, but some of the dialogue and situations feel more like a setup for the full game than something that has been completely developed on its own. I can see what the game is trying to establish, especially with the different people who become involved with Elisa, but I wanted more time with the characters before the prequel ended. That is probably the biggest thing stopping me from rating it higher.

What saves it for me is that the game is free, so I am not being asked to spend money on what is essentially a short introduction. I can go through the different branches, see how my choices change things and get a taste of the larger story without having to commit to anything. It is also easy to pick up and play because there are no complicated systems getting in the way. I just make choices, follow the story and see where things end up.

Overall, Elisa: The Innkeeper: Prequel is a decent short visual novel that has a few good ideas but clearly feels like an introduction rather than a complete experience. I like the unusual perspective, branching choices, colourful artwork and the way decisions can affect Elisa's future. The short length, limited character development and unfinished feeling keep it from reaching the higher ratings for me. Still, considering it is free and gives me several different branches to explore, I think it is worth trying if I already like choice based visual novels. It does enough to make me curious about the full story, but it does not give me enough content on its own to make it something I would rate extremely highly.

Rating: 6.9/10
